wa_cave_wall_2.blurb: Cave Wall is a bolted sport crag on Nason Ridge, in the Leavenworth part of the Central-East Cascades. Its main feature is a steep face that bends into a bulging overhang, and it sits right beside another wall in the same cluster, the Balcony. The 14 routes run from 5.10 up to 5.13, with most of them at 5.11 and 5.12, so it suits climbers already comfortable on hard, steep sport lines rather than anyone looking for moderates. Expect a short but steep uphill trail to reach the base.

wa_middle_wall.blurb: Middle Wall is the centerpiece of The Cave, a sport crag about halfway along the Tieton River canyon. It is a blocky face roughly 100 feet tall, with Mark's Wall to the left and the Oak Wall to the right. Nearly all of its 14 routes are bolted sport lines, with a single trad option, and almost everything is 5.11, plus a couple of low-to-mid 5.12s and one 5.10. Climbing is technical and varied: slopers, pinches, crimps, jugs, roofs and shallow stemming. The face points southeast, so it catches the morning sun and falls into shade by early afternoon in summer, and winter days can be workable. Reach it by hiking the main trail past Mark's Wall.

wa_main_wall_2.blurb: Main Wall is the principal cliff at Spring Mountain, a multi-pitch crag near Darrington. The face rises about five pitches, and only a few lines run all the way to the top. All 14 routes here are trad, mostly 5.9 and 5.10 with one 5.11, so it works well for climbers who want longer moderate-to-mid-grade routes. The bolts are there, but they are not full sport protection, so a rack is needed to protect sections of each route. A large overhang dominates the right side, while the left end sits in older forest and stays cooler. Traffic is light, which means moss can creep back over the routes.
wa_main_wall_2.approach: Follow the trail up from the pullout. After about 20 minutes a pair of cairns marks a fork: going left through them leads to the base of the wall, while continuing straight up reaches the big overhang section.

wa_fun_forest.blurb: Fun Forest is a small crag tucked beside I-90 near North Bend, east of Exit 47. Most of the 14 routes are trad, mainly cracks of different widths, with a handful of bolted lines mixed in. Grades start around 5.7 and reach 5.12, with a cluster at 5.11. It faces south, but it tends to stay damp for much of the year, so it works best as a quiet alternative when the busier North Bend crags are crowded. The freeway is close and loud. The approach is the novelty: you walk through a wildlife tunnel under the interstate, and the cliff is just on the far side.
wa_fun_forest.parking_note: Take Exit 47 and head back under the interstate, then follow forest road 9034 and fork onto 5800. Watch for the freeway tunnel on the left and pull off the road nearby; there is no lot.
wa_fun_forest.approach: Walk back to the wildlife tunnel under the freeway and go through it; the crag is just beyond. Bring a headlamp for the tunnel.

wa_alphabet_rock.blurb: Alphabet Rock is a small roadside crag in Icicle Canyon, near Leavenworth and close to Givler's Dome. It holds only a few routes, but they are a mix: mostly trad cracks, along with some sport lines, a top-rope and one aid line. Grades go from easy 5.6 up to 5.12, and 5.10 is the most common grade. The walk from the car is about a minute on an obvious trail, which keeps it popular for a quick session or a warm-up before heading deeper into the canyon. One line also doubles as a V2 boulder problem.

wa_obelisk_boulder_2.blurb: Obelisk Boulder is a cube-shaped block among the Deception Glade boulders, in the forest on the trail up to the Deception Crags near Exit 38 and North Bend. It sits directly uphill from the Lean-To Boulders, about 150 feet farther along the path toward SubStation Wall, so it is easy to fit in on the way to or from the crags. There are 14 problems spread over several faces. The grades run from V0 to V5, with most between V0 and V3 and a single harder problem, making it friendly to newer boulderers.

wa_2_recess_wall.blurb: Recess Wall is one of the Prospector Crags west of Mazama, in the Methow Valley. The cliff is slightly less than vertical and crossed by small roofs, and many routes start off ledges, which gives a mildly exposed feel. Of the 14 routes, 12 are sport and 2 are trad, running from 5.7 to 5.11, with most at 5.9 and 5.10. All the climbing faces south, so it is warmer than some nearby walls and can catch a breeze. The view down the valley is a big part of the appeal. Weather up here can turn worse than it looks in town.

wa_a_the_black_forest_slab.blurb: The Black Forest Slab is a tall, low-angle wall in the Little Si area near North Bend, grouped with World Wall 2. Its 14 routes are almost all bolted sport lines, plus one top-rope, and they span roughly 5.6 to 5.10, mainly 5.9 and 5.10. The climbing is friction-based with many tiny micro holds, a change of pace from the steep walls around it. Moss and pine needles build up quickly, so bring a brush. The base sits under a feature known as the shroom, reached by a hike of about 20 minutes that passes the top of Canopy Crag.

_conflicts.wa_obelisk_boulder_2: Stored rock is volcanic rock; the Deception Crags parent page (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105791955/deception-crags) calls the local stone metamorphic. Left unchanged and not named in the blurb.
